q: Compare last week's performance against this week and identify the likely causes.

checks.what: tool: compares against last week or same weekdays last week

answer:
Short answer — This week-to-date (2026-10-12..2026-10-14, partial) net sales are ₹182,618 vs last week (2026-10-05..2026-10-11) ₹645,654; orders 97 vs 339; ad spend ₹121,390 vs ₹430,736; net profit improved from -₹68,271 to -₹4,937. (Measured.)

Evidence
- Last week (2026-10-05..2026-10-11): Net sales ₹645,654 · Orders 339 · Ad spend ₹430,736 · Net profit -₹68,271. (Measured)
- This week so far (2026-10-12..2026-10-14, partial): Net sales ₹182,618 · Orders 97 · Ad spend ₹121,390 · Net profit -₹4,937. (Measured)

Why this happened — likely contributors (what the data shows)
- Fewer sessions and orders (measured): Sessions fell substantially and Orders are well below their usual range for comparable days — the diagnostics show Orders and Sessions are the largest arithmetic drivers of the drop in net sales. (Measured)
- Ad spend dropped and moved with performance (correlation): Ad spend is lower this week and the diagnostics flag it as correlated with the sales drop (tested as correlation, not proven causal). The engine did not find a firm causal link but marks ad spend as a likely contributor. (Measured → Correlation)
- Channel / mix shift reduced conversion (observed mix effect): the conversion-rate fell because volume shifted toward unattributed / “(not set)” traffic groups (a Simpson’s-paradox style mix shift) — this mix change reduced overall conversion even where per-group rates did not uniformly fall. (Measured / Derived)
- No single upstream cause proven: the causal diagnostic did not identify a single supported cause that passes causal tests; several measures moved together and the tool classified the relationships as correlation / insufficient evidence rather than confirmed causation. (Diagnosis result)

Context & data notes
- This week is partial (data through 14:00 IST on 2026-10-14) and was compared to the full prior week. Platform ad metrics refresh faster than commerce P&L; totals above are the order-date commerce view for sales/orders and paid_media for ad spend. (Data note)
